subject: Audit export / filter spec — confirmation + next steps
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Anita Shah <anita@novahealth.io>, Tom Rigsby <tom@novahealth.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Audit export / filter spec — confirmation + next steps

Hi Anita / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and three concrete asks so we can scope the engineering demo: 

1) Recap of requirements (as we understood them):
   - NovaHealth needs request/response audit exports for investigation and regulatory review.
   - Fields to include: timestamp, route/model, request-id/trace-id (hashed), request headers (with PII redaction), request body summary (token counts + pseudonymized ids), response status and response metadata — NOT full unredacted user text unless explicitly scoped.
   - Retention: 90 days in raw form for internal triage; 365 days for pseudonymized audit exports accessible to NovaHealth via secure export.
   - Residency: Audit exports must be stored in us-east-1 and available via S3-compatible export with KMS-managed keys owned by NovaHealth.

2) Redaction & hashing expectations:
   - Trace IDs: prefer deterministic hashing (SHA256 truncated) so NovaHealth can correlate events without seeing raw IDs.
   - Header-level masking: we will redact Authorization / Cookie / X-User-Phone / X-SSN headers by default; allow a configurable allowlist for non-sensitive headers.
   - Request/response bodies: we propose a "high-sensitivity" pipeline that tokenizes and pseudonymizes personally identifying tokens (emails, SSNs, phone numbers) and emits a redacted snippet.

3) Next steps we propose:
   - You: confirm the minimal fields you need in the audit export CSV/JSON (see attached draft spreadsheet).
   - Us: schedule a 45-minute engineering demo for the redaction configuration + export flow (we'll bring an engineer and a sample of redaction rules).
   - Legal: we'll share the SOC2 / encryption details and a residency appendix before the demo.

I've attached a draft "audit-filter-spec" spreadsheet that maps candidate fields to recommended default redaction behavior, and a small sample of how a redacted log line would look. Please review and flag any missing fields.

Proposed demo window: Tue 15 Sep 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 16 Sep 13:00–14:00 PT. Which works best?

Thanks —
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni

[vivek@redwood.com]

Subject: Re: Audit export / filter spec — confirmation + next steps

Vivek —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick clarifications from our compliance team: 

- Retention: we cannot have any raw free-text responses stored for more than 30 days unless they are explicitly redacted/pseudonymized. The 90/365 split you suggested is close, but we need raw retention capped at 30d. Pseudonymized exports can be retained longer (365d).
- Trace IDs: deterministic hashing is fine as long as keys are managed by NovaHealth (we want to ensure we can map across our systems). Can Redwood expose a key-rotation schedule for the hashing material?
- Residency: us-east-1 for storage + export gives us the coverage we need.

We reviewed the attached spreadsheet and added a comments column for three fields we need: request_user_email, billing_customer_id, and original_request_token (the last should always be redacted and never exported).

We can do Tue 15 Sep 10:00 PT for the demo. Please send calendar invite and an agenda so we can loop in our infra lead.

-Anita
Anita Shah
Director, Compliance & Privacy — NovaHealth Systems
Anita.Shah@novahealth.io

Folks —

Quick confirmation from infra: we can support the customer-managed KMS approach for hashing material and export keying. Notes: 

- Hashing: we'll implement a deterministic SHA256-based HMAC using a customer-provided key stored in their KMS. We will only store the HMAC output (truncated) and never persist the raw trace identifier. Key access will be via an assumed IAM role with restricted read-only permissions.
- Rotation: rotation is supported; we will provide a rotation window and re-hash strategy doc in the follow-up (DB migration is not required because HMAC depends on the key — we will record the key id/version along each exported row).
- Retention policy: software-wise we can TTL raw debug buffers to 30s, and persist only redacted/pseudonymized exports for the 365-day window.

I will attach a short note for the demo that shows sample HMAC outputs and an example S3 export record format.

-Karthik

Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
